newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit extends rise on central bank intervention.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit extends rise on central bank intervention.

text.p: * Ringgit rises further on central bank intervention and stop-loss dollar sales
* Bank Negara sells dollar/ringgit from 2.5050 to 2.4980 in Sydney
* Dollar bids out of Singapore seen at 2.5020
The ringgit extended its rise against the dollar in early Asian trading, helped by further central bank intervention, dealers said.
Dealers said Bank Negara sold the dollar from 2.5050 to 2.4980 ringgit this morning. The sales were done in Sydney through an agent bank, they said.
But dealers said the amount sold was not big.
"It may be less than $50 million," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.
Dealers said dollar/ringgit hit a low of 2.4950 this morning after the sales by Bank Negara, before buying by funds pushed it back up to above 2.50.
"There are dollar bids out of Singapore at 2.5020 and I think some funds are trying to push the dollar back up," said a Malaysian bank dealer.
He said dollar buying was unlikely to be aggressive due to fears of further intervention by the central bank.

Bank Negara sold large amounts of the dollar late on Tuesday as speculators were threatening to push dollar/ringgit above 2.5250, the level at which the central bank had aggressively defended the ringgit.
At 0215 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5025/35 to a dollar. It was at 2.5250 before the central bank's intervention on Tuesday.
